3bde36e29dd02d0b.text: Saturday, three in the morning. At three twelve the same provider goes down again, and the phone stays dark.

68b02ff1c7b62f36.text: Larkfield's apps no longer call providers directly. They call one door, a gateway. It checks who is asking, and it holds the provider keys, so the apps never do.

7e83dd0a01f99caf.text: So I can't paste a key I never had. Got it.

5e4fc9a8f9b3058a.text: Follow one call. The support app sends a question with the name support. That name is an alias, Larkfield's own name for a job. The gateway looks it up in its table.

db86d096cd21f7bc.text: The table says provider A first, then provider B. Provider A is down, so the gateway sends the call to provider B, with the provider key that only the gateway holds.

6f07216596addfed.text: Provider B answers. The gateway passes the answer back and writes one line in its log: the team, the alias and the tokens used, one thousand eight hundred and fifty. A token is a small piece of text that providers bill by.

531129ea57214dd8.text: At the end of the month, Finance reads the log and adds the rows up by team. The one number on the invoice now has a name beside every part of it.

246e65d1ab819f01.text: Every line has a name. I could get used to this.

0d03604d1e852ce3.text: One thing is now easy. Every app asks for support, never for a model. When a better model comes out, the platform team changes one line of the table, and no app changes.

cd1362c82495a40d.text: So I can try the new model today? Today today?

d29f2b7eccc0d365.text: Next come four short games on what you have just seen. Then the first lab, where you send calls to a real gateway and watch what it does with them.
